svg.title: Physical radar and implemented simulation signal-processing pipelines
svg.desc: Two aligned signal-processing pipelines compare a representative physical four-face phased-array radar with this demo's simplified implementation. The figure identifies omitted element-domain processing and quantifies the exact implemented RawReturn and dwell-integration rates.
svg.text: Representative physical processing versus the exact simplified DDS demo path
same modeled aperture, bandwidth, range window, and PRF · processing order varies by architecture

g.text: ELEMENT-DOMAIN WORKLOAD · 2.736 billion complex range samples / second
This is the physical sample-count scale before the element channels are combined.

g.aria-label: Focus illustrative physical element data rate
g.text: assumes one 16-bit I + one 16-bit Q value per gated complex sample; payload only
Wider operational bandwidths, oversampling, extra beams, and framing can raise this substantially.
Element RF, ADC, channel calibration, beamforming arithmetic, Doppler filtering, adaptive clutter processing, and monopulse are not executed.

svg.text: exact rates and simplifications in the current source

g.text: The implementation starts after beamforming: four streams
replace 4,096 element channels. Complex-sample workload is
Ten 1 kHz pulse returns become one 100 Hz dwell trace per
face. Thresholding and tracking reduce the flow again from
dense range arrays to sparse measurements and state vectors.

g.aria-label: Focus RF carrier versus digital data-rate explanation
g.text: 3 GHz IS NOT THE DIGITAL DATA RATE
The RF carrier is downconverted. Bandwidth, receive-window
samples, channel count, quantization, and beam count set the
processing rate. This diagram uses the demo's 1 MHz model.

svg.text: Rates are decimal SI payload rates. The physical lane is an engineering reference using public round-number assumptions, not an operational-system claim.
